First, Look Closely

The Grill Is Working All Day at CHAMOS

Watch an arepa come off the grill at CHAMOS and you will see it right away. The corn cake is crisp at the edges, soft in the middle, and opened up while it is still steaming. Then it gets filled deep, with chicken, shredded beef, cheese or avocado, until it barely closes. That is not fast food pretending to be homemade. That is a family recipe, made by hand, one order at a time.

So why does most food on the road taste exactly the same, while this sits right here in Charlotte, waiting?

You have done the burgers. You have done the drive thru line. Scroll down and look at the plates below, up close, and ask yourself why you have not tried the one thing on this page yet.

The Proof Is on the Plate

Look at This Food, Up Close

Here Is the Thing

Most People Never Try It. Then They Are Hooked.

Plenty of Charlotte drivers pass Venezuelan food every single week without stopping, and it is not because they would not love it. It is because nobody ever showed them what an arepa really is, up close, the way you just saw it. One bite of a hot corn cake stuffed with chicken, beef or cheese, and the mystery is over.

That is the moment people come back with friends. The food was never the problem. Never seeing it was.

Who Is Behind the Grill

One Family. Two Spots. Zero Shortcuts.

CHAMOS Grill is a family owned Venezuelan restaurant in Charlotte, North Carolina. We serve the food we grew up on, from arepas and cachapas hot off the grill to a full Pabellón Criollo plate. Find us at our restaurant on Monroe Road or at our food truck on The Plaza, and come hungry.
